title: Trajectory sync: hypotheses & tradeoffs (prep)
content:
Context:
- Product asked for a compact plan to hit a mid-Q milestone: reduce p95 token cost by ~18% while keeping per-response latency within current SLO (p95 <= 320ms for 512 tokens workload).
- Attendees: product (Maya), eng (Jordan + Ravi), applied-ML (Ana), infra (Samir).
- This doc is a personal prep + agenda for the cross-functional alignment sync. Intended to be terse — we’ll expand into confluence after decisions.

Meeting goals (90m):
1) Surface candidate hypotheses for cost/latency wins (batching/caching/quantization/route changes).
2) Align on 1 prioritized experiment to run as a canary next sprint + measurement plan.
3) Capture roll-back/fallback policy & owner list so customer-facing teams can be confident.

Pre-reads (please scan before sync):
- Perf cohort microbench (Ana): key graphs for model A/B token latency by sequence length. Link in artifacts.
- Current routing policy doc (Samir): how requests choose hosted vs dedicated variants.
- Jira tickets: JIRA-ENG-872 (runtime batching tweaks), JIRA-PROD-1294 (product acceptance criteria).

Working hypotheses (short):
H1: Small increases to continuous batch windows (10->15ms) will drop per-token cost by 6–9% on high-concurrency customers with <50 tokens median, with negligible p95 impact when combined with adaptive batching.
H2: Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts will yield large gains for certain customers (30% cost drop) but only if we can pin cold-start mem usage under 2GB per worker. Risk: cache invalidation complexity.
H3: 4-bit quantization (Q4 with per-channel scale) on our mid-size model reduces memory & GPU footprint enabling higher packing density, but may introduce a 1-3% quality regression on domain prompts — need eval set.
H4: Route-by-price (send low-tier to quantized variant by default) reduces unit cost but raises oddball quality/regression support load for CS.

Data we need to validate hypotheses: (owner)
- H1: latency distribution by arrival pattern and current batching windows (Jordan) — sample traces + simulated microbench.
- H2: prefix repeat-rate by customer (Product/CS + infra logs) — show top 20 customers where repeats > 10%. (Maya)
- H3: eval comparison on our regression suite + customer-provided golden prompts (Ana) — baseline vs Q4.
- H4: customer tolerance mapping (support tickets + SLA clauses) to inform acceptable risk (Maya + CS).

Quick experiment proposals (pick 1):
A) Adaptive batching pilot (H1): 2-week canary on 2 low-risk customers; modify batch window to 15ms with fallback at 25ms; metrics: per-token cost, p95 latency, error rate. (owner: Jordan).
B) KV-prefix cache pilot (H2): enable cache for 1 customer flow that shows high repeat-rate; set TTL 10m; measure hit-rate and GPU memory delta. (owner: Samir + Ana).
C) Quantized route experiment (H3+H4): expose a quantized variant behind a feature-flag; route 5% of low-priority traffic; run blind eval for quality regressions. (owner: Ana).

Tradeoffs snapshot (notes to self, to surface in convo):
- Speed vs accuracy: quantization wins cost but needs human-in-loop eval; need a rollback trigger for >1.5% regression on core evals.
- Operational complexity: caching + routing increases stateful components — needs SRE runbook and incident playbook.
- Customer trust: any experiment that degrades deterministic outputs (e.g., quantization) must be limited to non-critical customers or have opt-in.

Risk ladder & mitigations: (short)
- Regression detected in evals -> block rollout; require staged ramp & automated quality checks (Ana).
- Memory blowups from caching -> apply per-worker guardrails and circuit-breaker (Samir).
- Latency spike from larger batches under low concurrency -> adaptive fallback to single-request path (Jordan).

Discussion prompts for Product/Eng/ML:
- Product: which customer segments are acceptable for canaries? Recommend: internal customers + 3 consenting external small customers.
- Eng: what is the infra readiness for stateful caching in hosted plane (Samir)? How much dev effort to add safe guards? Rough estimate: 2 sprints + 1 SRE sprint to harden.
- ML: can we run Q4 offline evals on the top-10 customer prompt sets in 3 days? If not, what’s the blocker?

Decision points we need end-of-sync:
- Select the experiment (A/B/C).
- Owners + 1-week runway to prepare artifacts.
- Acceptance criteria (must-have metrics & regression thresholds).

Action items (owner / due):
- Jordan: produce latency dist (arrival-patterned) and proposed batch-window patch PR. Due 2026-06-30. -> create JIRA-ENG-880.
- Ana: run quantization eval on core regression suite + 10 customer prompt sets; produce pass/fail table. Due 2026-06-29.
- Samir: sketch caching architecture and guardrails (memory limits, eviction, circuit-breaker). Due 2026-07-01.
- Maya: confirm 3 consenting customers for canary + sign-off criteria. Due 2026-06-28.
- Ravi (me): draft confluence experiment spec with rollback playbook & communication plan. Due 2026-06-30.

Notes-to-self / scratch (informal):
- Keep experiment narrow: one change at a time to attribute wins.
- Mention legal/compliance if we persist customer prompts in cache long-term (Maya).
- Think about billing visibility: need token-level cost telemetry during pilot (Product + Finance).
- If quantization looks marginal (0.5% regression), consider mixing: route 20% to quantized + 80% to baseline and use reranking to compensate.

Follow-ups & next sync:
- Weekly check-ins: Tue 30m standup for experiment owners (start 2026-06-29).
- Decision review meeting: 2026-07-06 to approve larger rollout if pilot meets criteria.

Open questions to bring up live:
- What is acceptable quality delta for accounting features (e.g., codegen correctness)? (Product)
- Are there customers who explicitly forbid feature-flagged routing? (CS/legal)
- Any infra quotas in cloud provider that block more packing of model instances? (Infra)

Bottom line (one-liner to lead with at sync):
We have 3 credible levers (batching, caching, quantization). Pick one focused pilot this sprint, instrument with clear quality gates, and ensure rollback & comms baked in before ramp.

-- end of prep scratch --

(If time in meeting: sketch quick experiment timeline on whiteboard: week0 prep, week1 canary, week2 ramp/stop. Keep notes here.)
